title: Construction milestones reached at fourth Zhangzhou unit
html:
The Hualong One reactor design features a double-layered containment building, the main function of which is to ensure the integrity and leak tightness of the reactor building, and it plays a key role in the containment of radioactive substances.

On 26 November, the inner dome - with an inner diameter of about 46 metres and a total lifting weight of about 470 tonnes - was hoisted at an elevation of approximately 45 metres using a 3,200-tonne crawler crane.


(Image: CNNC)

"This hoisting operation fully utilised the mature construction experience of units 1 to 3 of the Zhangzhou Nuclear Power Plant, employing proven dome construction methods," China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) said. "This marks the transition from civil construction to equipment installation, laying a solid foundation for subsequent installation, commissioning, and grid connection. This is another important achievement in the batch construction of nuclear power in China."

The installation of the inner dome at Zhangzhou 4 follows the hoisting of the final steam generator into place through the open top of the containment building on 20 November. Steam generators are used in pressurised water reactors to transfer heat from the reactor coolant into water in a secondary circuit, producing the steam used to power the electricity-generating turbines. Each steam generator contains thousands of kilometres of tubes through which hot water flows.


(Image: CNNC)

Zhangzhou unit 4 features ZH-65-type steam generators - each weighing 365 tonnes and measuring over 21 metres in length - independently designed by the China Nuclear Power Institute and manufactured by Dongfang Electric.


(Image: CNNC)

"The ZH-65 steam generator of Hualong One, as a major component of the primary loop pressure boundary, is one of the most critical pieces of equipment in the unit," CNNC said. "It is the first domestically developed third-generation nuclear power steam generator with completely independent intellectual property rights, and its high-tech design and manufacturing represent the forefront of China's high-end manufacturing industry."

The Zhangzhou plant

Zhangzhou 4 is the fourth Hualong One unit to be built at the site. Construction of Zhangzhou 1 began in October 2019, with that of unit 2 starting in September 2020. Unit 1 entered commercial operation on 1 January last year, followed by unit 2 on 1 January this year. In September 2022, China's State Council approved the construction of two Hualong One units as Phase II - units 3 and 4 - of the Zhangzhou plant. Construction of unit 3 began in February last year, with that of unit 4 starting in September last year.

There are plans for two more Hualong One units at the plant. Once fully completed, a six-unit Zhangzhou plant would provide more than 60 billion kilowatt-hours of clean energy annually, estimated to meet 75% of the total electricity consumption of Xiamen and Zhangzhou cities in southern Fujian.

The Zhangzhou project - with a total investment of over CNY100 billion (USD14 billion) - is owned by CNNC-Guodian Zhangzhou Energy Company, a joint venture between CNNC (51%) and China Energy Investment Corporation (CHN Energy) (49%).
summary: The inner safety dome has been installed on the containment building of unit 4 at the Zhangzhou nuclear power plant, the fourth of six Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors planned for the site in China's Fujian province.
